findings.issue: The guard validates value.asset._ref but passes the complete untrusted value to the SDK. The actual SDK gives top-level _ref/_id and asset.url precedence over that nested validated reference. Consequently the generated image can have a different ID, unsupported format or out-of-policy dimensions while imagePresentation still derives normalization from the original nested asset._ref. parseHome accepts the complete document instead of selecting canonical fallback.
findings.reproduction: Executed actual adapter and canonical home source transpiled only in memory, with real installed SDK1.2.0 and retained otherwise-valid synthetic document. Control clean document accepts normally. Add hero.photo.asset.url='https://cdn.sanity.io/images/zhn2ddaj/production/' + 'b'.repeat(40) + '-1200x800.svg', leaving the validated nested asset._ref as original valid PNG: parseHome(doc,'en') remains non-null and emits the different .svg URL with rect120,40,1020,680. Alternatively add hero.photo._ref='image-'+'b'.repeat(40)+'-900000x900000-jpg': it remains accepted and emits900000x900000 URL/rect90000,45000,765000,765000 with position0%0%, despite the guarded nested1200x800PNG reference. No remote request, source change, CMS mutation or image serving was performed.
findings.impact: Demonstrated violation of the explicit safe supported-reference/dimension validation and whole-document invalid-media fallback contract.
